kept.excerpt: The Simplex/CBN stimulated first-round poll put Raquel Lyra at 45% and João Campos at 37.9%, with 11.1% unable or unwilling to answer and 4.6% choosing blank, null or none. In a two-candidate scenario, Lyra had 46.4% and Campos 39.9%. The survey interviewed 1,067 voters by telephone on September 16–20, 2026, with a three-percentage-point margin of error and 95% confidence, and was registered as PE-07901/2026.
kept.relevance: This cutoff-day poll supplies the most recent verified fieldwork in the pack and measures both first-round and head-to-head support.

kept.excerpt: João Campos's campaign was trying to secure a visit by President Lula to Pernambuco before the first round, but Lula had not confirmed it. Although Lula had declared support for Campos, the report described a non-aggression pact with Governor Raquel Lyra. Campos's allies regarded a presidential visit as decisive given his disadvantage in polling.
kept.relevance: This cutoff-day report identifies the status and limits of presidential campaign support and a potential remaining campaign catalyst.

kept.excerpt: AtlasIntel measured Raquel Lyra at 48.7% and João Campos at 45.6% in the first round. Its runoff simulation put Lyra at 51.1% and Campos at 47.3%, described as a technical tie within the poll's two-percentage-point margin of error. The Bloomberg-commissioned survey recruited 1,793 voters digitally on September 11–16, with 95% confidence, and was registered as PE-02989/2026.
kept.relevance: This recent independent poll tests whether Campos was competitive in both rounds using a different collection method.

kept.excerpt: RealTime Big Data put João Campos at 44% and Raquel Lyra at 43% in the stimulated first round. Both candidates had 44% in the runoff simulation, with 6% choosing blank or null and 6% not knowing or not answering. The poll interviewed 1,600 people in Pernambuco on September 10–14, 2026, with a two-percentage-point margin of error and 95% confidence, under registration PE-07953/2026.
kept.relevance: This poll provides a materially different reading from surveys showing Lyra ahead and helps assess disagreement across pollsters.

kept.excerpt: Datafolha put Raquel Lyra at 47% and João Campos at 42%, a technical tie within its three-percentage-point margin of error. Excluding blank, null and undecided responses, Lyra had 51% of valid votes and Campos 46%; a runoff simulation gave Lyra 51% and Campos 44%. The Folha/TV Globo survey interviewed 1,204 voters in 48 municipalities on September 8–10 and was registered under PE-04411/2026 and BR-05923/2026.
kept.relevance: This major poll measures both the risk of a first-round decision and Campos's position in a possible runoff.

kept.excerpt: Quaest put Raquel Lyra at 43% and João Campos at 37%, compared with 44% and 36%, respectively, in its August 25 release. Undecided voters accounted for 12%, while blank, null and non-voting responses totaled 6%. The Globo-commissioned poll interviewed 1,302 Pernambuco voters on September 4–7, with a three-percentage-point margin of error and 95% confidence, and was registered as PE-00285/2026. Rejection was 40% for Campos and 34% for Lyra.
kept.relevance: This independent survey adds trend, undecided-voter and rejection evidence relevant to Campos's ability to close the gap.

kept.excerpt: The 2026 general election was scheduled for October 4, including elections for governors. Any second round was scheduled for October 25. First-round free electoral advertising on radio and television was scheduled to begin August 28 and end October 1.
kept.publisher: Tribunal Regional Eleitoral de Santa Catarina
kept.relevance: This dated official electoral-court announcement establishes the election timetable and remaining campaign window.

kept.excerpt: With all 3,409 polling sections totaled, João Campos of the PSB was reelected mayor of Recife in the first round of the 2024 municipal election. He received 725,721 votes, equivalent to 78.11% of valid votes.
kept.relevance: Campos's official prior electoral performance establishes the strength of his Recife base, while covering a narrower electorate than the statewide contest.

search_notes: Frozen evidence cutoff: 2026-09-21 inclusive. Included eight dated items, with five distinct polling series, cutoff-day campaign reporting, an official schedule and an official historical result; no forecast probability is supplied. Excerpts are factual English translations or paraphrases of Portuguese source text. Dates and figures were checked against source-specific web_search results containing publication timestamps and article text. web_fetch failed because multiple providers were registered; the requested agent-reach web read fallback returned RATE_LIMITED, so direct page retrieval was unavailable and indexed text was used. Later-dated reports, undated live pages, prediction-market pages and election-outcome material were excluded. The TSE calendar article was excluded because its current version showed an update after the cutoff; a dated regional electoral-court announcement was used instead. The historical TSE item shows an update on 2025-02-22, also before the cutoff. The September 17 Atlas article contains a weekday/day inconsistency in its body; its explicit publication timestamp and September 11–16 fieldwork were used.
